messages:
adele (sales): Heads-up — Concorde Bank wants a 2-week POC to validate streaming SDK + function/tool-calls and structured JSON output. They also sent a security questionnaire (SAML + KMS + audit logs). Can we assemble an SE + infra pair?

carlos (SE): I can take lead on the SDK/integration side. Quick clarifying q's from my side: do they want SSE or WebSocket for the streaming pipe? And do they need callbacks (tool calls) back into their infra?

adele (sales): They prefer SSE for simplicity, but said they'd accept a short-lived websocket if we need bi-directional callbacks. They want tool-calls to invoke an internal webhook for step-up auth flows.

carlos (SE): OK. Plan: I’ll prepare a minimal runbook + sample repo with 1) SSE ingestion using the JS SDK, 2) function-calling example that posts to a webhook, 3) structured output schema validation. Will use ephemeral creds for the POC.

carlos (SE): Sample SSE client snippet I'll include in the repo:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const stream = client.stream({ model: 'gpt-4-realtime', mode: 'sse' });
stream.on('message', (m) => { console.log('chunk', m); });
stream.send({ prompt: 'Summarize tx 123', functions: [{ name: 'stepup', url: 'https://concorde-hook.example/stepup' }] });
```

carlos (SE): For tool/function calling we should demo a signed webhook handshake (HMAC) and a fallback to a secure polling endpoint in case the webhook is blocked by their network.

sam (eng-infra): I can provision a short-lived dedicated instance (small GPU) for the POC if they want deterministic latency. Otherwise hosted with reserved throughput burst should be fine. Which direction do we want to go?

adele (sales): Concorde asked about hosted vs reserved cost for a 2-week POC. They want an estimate and whether any enterprise contract is required.

jamie (product): Pricing guidance: for a 2-week POC we typically offer hosted usage billing by token + a temporary trial burst allowance. If they require Dedicated capacity we can offer a time-limited dev reservation (monthly prorated) — estimate: ~ $X/day for small reserved pool. I'll DM finance for exact quote.

noah (security): On the questionnaire: we need to answer SAML SSO support, KMS integrations (customer-managed keys), audit log retention, IP allowlist, network egress controls, and SOC2 compliance docs. For POC, confirm whether they need on-prem or VPC private control plane.

carlos (SE): Quick checklist I'll include in runbook for the customer:
- SDK sample (JS + Python) for SSE streaming
- Function-call example with HMAC verification header sample
- Structured output schema JSON + validator snippet
- Minimal test harness to replay requests and assert deterministic outputs

carlos (SE): Structured output example (shape we'll validate):
```json
{
  "transaction_id": "string",
  "risk_score": "number",
  "steps": [ { "action": "string", "timestamp": "ISO8601" } ]
}
```

adele (sales): They also asked about data retention during POC and whether logs are accessible for debugging.

sam (eng-infra): For POC we can enable a short 30-day retention and grant read-only access to a workspace. Logs can be sanitized before sharing. If they insist on no data leaving their VPC, we should propose Private variant (VPC or on-prem).

carlos (SE): For the webhook tool-call portion I'll add a sample verify flow: `X-Redwood-Signature` HMAC-SHA256 over payload; sample code for verify in Python will be in repo.

noah (security): I'll start answering the questionnaire. For KMS: we support external KMS via customer key wrap; I'll attach the short KMS integration doc. For SAML: we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows; need entityID + ACS URL from them.

adele (sales): Great. Next steps: Carlos & Sam to ship runbook + repo by EOD tomorrow. Noah to kick off questionnaire answers and flag any blockers. Jamie please confirm pricing estimate before EOD. I'll book a kickoff call with the Concorde POC team for Mon 09:00 PT.

carlos (SE): Will do. I'll include a tiny demo app that posts to a temporary webhook and shows structured output validation result.

sam (eng-infra): I'll pre-config a dev reservation and share creds (ephemeral) to test ingress/egress.

dev-bot: Deploy triggered for project/concorde-poc (env: staging). Build 20260321-87 queued. :rocket:

noah (security): Flag: if they require HSM-backed KMS and FIPS endpoints, that will need eng-infra lead time — calling this out early.

jamie (product): Pricing note: if POC expands into a pilot >30 days, we should transition to a short-term reserved plan to avoid unexpected throttling. I'll include that in the quote.

adele (sales): Thanks all — I'll send calendar invite and paste Concorde contact in thread after the call is booked.

carlos (SE): Added checklist PR to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-concorde (private). Will drop a minimal runbook link here once ready.

adele (sales): (added Concorde contact) -- Lukasz (l.koz@concordebank.com) and Priya (p.n@concordebank.com). Ok to loop them in after runbook is shared. :+1:

sam (eng-infra): Confirmed: reserved dev instance ready; credentials will be rotated daily.

carlos (SE): End-to-end test plan in runbook: 1) stream request -> 2) function call to webhook -> 3) webhook returns stepup token -> 4) structured JSON validated. If any step fails, fallback to polling path.

adele (sales): Perfect — thanks.
